line_items.reasoning: FDX cut the top end of FY25 adjusted EPS guidance from $22 to $21 (new range implied lower midpoint), directly signaling results and outlook fell short of the $20–$22 range guided last quarter.

Weaker-than-expected demand (soft B2B/industrial volumes, USPS contract loss creating a ~$500M headwind starting Q2, and yield pressure) undermines the low-to-mid single digit growth trajectory guided for FY25.

Q1 adjusted operating profit declined $382M YoY, and incremental headwinds (USPS loss ~$500M, international yield pressure now $500M vs. prior $400M, higher purchase transportation costs) more than offset DRIVE savings, putting the ~15% YoY operating income growth target at risk.
No information was provided in Q1 results indicating CapEx deviated from the guided $5.2B for FY25, so this is treated as on-track.
FDX completed the guided $1B in Q1 share repurchases on schedule and announced an additional $1B buyback for Q2, exceeding the pace implied by the $2.5B full-year plan.
